Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in women, but in terms of mortality, lung cancer has historically been the leading cause of cancer death among women in the U.S. This is because lung cancer tends to be more deadly and is often diagnosed at a later stage.

Colon cancer and cervical cancer cause fewer deaths compared to lung and breast cancer. Skin cancer, while common, generally has a high survival rate.

According to the most recent statistics from reputable sources like the American Cancer Society, lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death among women, surpassing breast cancer.
